installed_by_this_task.name: rome-hotel-taxes
installed_by_this_task.command: claude mcp add rome-hotel-taxes --scope project -- python3 /home/batnini/mimo-agents/rome-2star/worker_c/rome_hotel_taxes_mcp.py
installed_by_this_task.note: no pre-existing MCP server was uninstalled or modified; the list before and after differs by exactly this one addition

verdict.why: It is the only source that satisfies the wording of the requirement literally: named, separate tax positions ('10 % VAT' and 'City tax' as distinct line items with b_type percentage__included / per_person_per_night__included), the explicit provider statement 'Includes taxes and fees' with b_is_all_included=1, and the tax-inclusive stay total (b_total_price) — plus empty b_conditional_charges / b_nonmandatory_charges, i.e. proof that nothing is left to pay at the property.
verdict.prerequisite: The aws-waf-token that trvl already harvests through Booking's own browser flow and caches in ~/.trvl/cookies/www.booking.com.json. No API key, no captcha solving, no IP rotation. If the token is absent the script refuses to run rather than guessing.
verdict.recommended_fallback: Google Hotels 'AtySUc' (installed as MCP 'rome-hotel-taxes') — keyless, never contacts booking.com, so no WAF at all, 4.75 s per Rome 2-star search. It yields base/tax/fees/total per OTA channel but as ONE tax bucket, not as named VAT vs. city-tax lines.
verdict.cross_validation: The two paths agree to the cent (Melting Pot Rome: Google base 44.18 + tax 7.92 = total 52.10 == Booking net 44.1818 + VAT 4.42 + City tax 3.50 = total 52.1000000000001).
rejected: pricewin — aggregates 6 OTAs but exposes no tax field whatsoever
skiplagged — taxesAndFeesInDollars is null for every Rome 2-star property checked
stays — reaches the right data but its includes_taxes_and_fees flag is dead code (11/11 false)
trvl — booking path still WAF-blocked; Agoda path gives only an undifferentiated tax sum
all npm hotel MCPs — require RAPIDAPI_KEY / SERPAPI_API_KEY / HASDATA_API_KEY
verdict.recommended_booking_flow: 1) google_tax_probe.py / MCP rome-hotel-taxes for the cheap 2-star candidate list (WAF-free). 2) booking_breakdown.py for the final 1-3 candidates to obtain the named VAT / City-tax lines and the 'Includes taxes and fees' proof. 3) Pace booking.com requests at ~2.5 s; it answers 502 after ~20 rapid hits.

limitations: Rome 2-star hotels have no resort fee; the provider line vocabulary is '10 % VAT' + 'City tax' (+ Booking's aggregate 'sum included'). A 'resort fee' line does not exist in the Rome data — the guarantee one can give is 'taxes and fees are included in this total and nothing is left to pay at the property', not 'a specific resort fee is inside this number'.

Booking's City-tax line is typed 'per_person_per_night__included', so its amount depends on the occupancy that was requested (1 guest here). The 1-night figures are per stay; 2-night totals scale accordingly (verified: Google base 197.78 / tax 40.77 / total 238.55 for 2 nights).

Booking publishes the breakdown only when a room is actually bookable for the requested dates: Hotel Viminale with 2 nights / 2 adults returned 0 breakdowns, and Hotel Ferraro had no bookable room for 31.10.-01.11.2026 (Google still showed a rate for it).
Booking rate-limits: after roughly 20 rapid property-page fetches from this IP the same request returns HTTP 502 (2894 bytes) until the cooldown passes. With ~2.5 s pacing it returns 200 again.

The 2-star selection is made in Google Hotels (star_class == 2) and cross-checked per hotel against Booking's own 'RoomTableQueryResult:{}.stars' where Booking populates it (it was 2 for Hotel Benedetto, Hotel Lodi, Hotel Demetra, Hotel Adriatic, Hotel Ferraro; for the remaining properties Booking left that field empty, so only Google's class is available).

Booking's own star-class URL filter does not work any more in the new frontend: with stars=2 the Apollo store shows filters:{} and the result set still contains Mama Shelter and Hilton Rome; the 2-star restriction therefore cannot be delegated to Booking's search.
The upstream 'stays' package is NOT modified — its includes_taxes_and_fees flag stays broken. The fix lives in the separate 'rome-hotel-taxes' MCP server and in worker_c/google_tax_probe.py.
The aws-waf-token in ~/.trvl/cookies/www.booking.com.json is machine-local and can expire; booking_breakdown.py then exits with exit code 2 and an explicit message instead of returning wrong data.
No hotel prices were obtained via web search — web search was used only for code/server/endpoint research (trvl forks, MCP server manifests, provider endpoint documentation).
